title: AgentSec Dashboard Rollup
description: The normalised batch rollup: the one shape every output renders from, and the contract a Live Artifact or MCP App may depend on. Produced by reporting.normalizer.normalize_batch, written by `agentsec report --format json`, and returned by agentsec_start_run and agentsec_generate_report. Every field here is a verdict or a count derived from committed contracts; nothing the system under test emitted reaches this document. Per-run observations live behind agentsec://runs/{run_id} and its evidence resource, which carry their own redaction envelope.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this shape. The major component changes when a consumer would break; see reporting.publish.PUBLISH_SCHEMA_VERSION.

profile.description: The profile the rollup was filtered to, or "all" when the caller named none. A report headed with a profile it never filtered on is the mislabelling this field exists to avoid.

verdict_counts.description: Histogram over the runs counted, keyed by purple verdict.

axis_counts.description: The four-axis rollup. `not_tested` is a first-class outcome: an axis a scenario never asserted is never counted as a pass.

exit_code.description: 1 when any counted run is blocking. This is the CI gate.

provenance_counts.description: How many counted runs were proven against a replayed fixture versus a live system. Additive in 1.1: absent on documents produced before provenance existed, so a consumer must not assume it is present.

fixture_derived.description: True when every counted run's evidence is `recorded` — the whole rollup was proven against replayed fixtures, not a live attack. Drives the banner a reader must see before trusting a `secure` count. False on an empty batch.

superseded_runs.description: Stored runs older than the ones counted here. The rollup keeps the latest run per (scenario, target) so a scenario that failed fifty times last month cannot dominate today's picture; this field keeps the document honest that the history exists.

history.description: Per-scenario verdict timeline, oldest first, for trend rendering.

verdict.description: Highest rung reached, in precedence order error > detection_gap > prevention_gap > evidence_gap > response_gap > secure. A silent failure always outranks a noisy one.

blocking.description: Whether this run fails the CI gate: the scenario's gate is blocking and the profile blocks this verdict.

failed_checks.description: Only the checks that failed or errored. `assertion` and `observed` are evaluator-authored and quote values declared in the scenario contract.

collector_errors.description: A collector that could not answer. Present because an axis it fed degrades to `error` rather than to `pass`.

provenance.description: How this run's evidence was actually produced. Presentation only — never changes purple_verdict or any axis. Additive in 1.1; absent on documents produced before provenance existed.

evidence.description: recorded: every contributing source was file-backed (a replayed fixture). live: every contributing source queried a live system. mixed: some of each — named rather than hidden.

backends.description: Collector name -> backend kind, for collectors that actually contributed. Backend kinds only, never an endpoint or credential.
